Too short to see Jesus. So he climbed a tree. 🌳 Luke 19:1-10

Zacchaeus was the chief tax collector in Jericho, rich, and “little of stature.” He climbed a sycamore just to get a look. Jesus stopped right under that tree: “Zaccheus, make haste, and come down; for to day I must abide at thy house” (Luke 19:5). Everyone grumbled. Zacchaeus gave half his goods to the poor. “For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost” (Luke 19:10).

Has Jesus ever called your name when you felt farthest away? 👇

No armor. No sword. Just a sling and the living God. 🪨 1 Samuel 17

For forty days Goliath of Gath mocked Israel, and the whole army was “dismayed, and greatly afraid.” Then a young shepherd showed up with five smooth stones: “Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to thee in the name of the Lord of hosts” (1 Samuel 17:45). One stone. “For the battle is the Lord’s” (1 Samuel 17:47).

What giant are you facing this week? Name it, and let's pray 👇

700 left-handed slingers who never missed. It's in the Bible. 🎯

Hidden details #5: seven hundred chosen men who could “sling stones at an hair breadth, and not miss” (Judges 20:16), Elijah outrunning Ahab's chariot (1 Kings 18:46), three men who walked out of the furnace without even the smell of fire (Daniel 3:27), Absalom caught by his head in an oak (2 Samuel 18:9), and Jesus' sweat “as it were great drops of blood” in Gethsemane (Luke 22:44).

Which one did you already know? Comment 1 to 5 👇

Jesus showed up four days late. Then He called a dead man out of the tomb. 🪨 John 11

Lazarus was sick. Jesus waited two more days. When He arrived, Lazarus had been in the grave four days. Martha: “Lord, if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died” (John 11:21). Jesus: “I am the resurrection, and the life” (John 11:25). Then He wept. Then He cried with a loud voice, “Lazarus, come forth” (John 11:43).

Praying was against the law. He opened his window anyway. 🦁 Daniel 6

Rival officials got King Darius to sign a decree: pray to anyone but the king for thirty days, and you go to the lions. Daniel went home, “his windows being open in his chamber toward Jerusalem, he kneeled upon his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did aforetime” (Daniel 6:10). Next morning: “My God hath sent his angel, and hath shut the lions’ mouths” (Daniel 6:22).

When's your prayer time: morning, lunch, or night? 👇
